relevance.rationale: Technique, not a result the folio can consume as-is. The folio's conj:q-plancherel-asymptotic-skeleton has an explicitly OPEN part (3): weak convergence of the q-deformed Wedderburn measure mu_n^(q) for q != 1, which it names as 'q-deformed Kerov-Vershik convergence'. This paper proves exactly that pair of statements — limit shape (first order, extending Vershik-Kerov/Logan-Shepp) and Gaussian fluctuations (second order, extending Kerov's CLT) — for the JACK (alpha) deformation of Plancherel measure, with the polynomiality of Jack-character structure constants as the engine. The alpha-deformation is NOT the folio's q-deformation (Jack deforms the hook product j_lambda^(alpha); the folio deforms via quantum dimensions dim_q^2/[n]_q!), so nothing here discharges part (3). What it supplies is a worked template for the same theorem in a one-parameter deformation, from an author already cited in the block (feray2010 backs part (2); feray-meliot2012 is the q-Plancherel CLT). Corpus-grep: no ref() entry, no 'Jack' entry, no 'Gaussian fluctuation' match.

keyResults.locator: §1.1 eq. (1) + main theorem (bulk first- and second-order asymptotics)
keyResults.statement: Under the Jack deformation P_n^(alpha)(lambda) = alpha^n n!/j_lambda^(alpha) of Plancherel measure, the bulk of a random Young diagram has a deterministic limit shape and Gaussian second-order fluctuations, extending Vershik-Kerov/Logan-Shepp and Kerov to all alpha > 0.
keyResults.useForFolio: A precedent theorem of exactly the shape conj:q-plancherel-asymptotic-skeleton part (3) needs, in a sibling one-parameter deformation. Cite as the method template and as evidence that the deformed-Kerov-Vershik statement is reachable; do NOT present it as covering the q-deformed weight.

keyResults.locator: §1 (main tool: polynomiality of structure constants of Jack characters, after Lassalle)
keyResults.statement: The structure constants of Jack characters are polynomial in the deformation parameter, which is what makes the cumulant/CLT machinery go through.
keyResults.useForFolio: Identifies the structural input a q-analogue would have to reproduce for the folio's part (3): a polynomiality/degree bound on the structure constants of the q-deformed characters. Names the obstacle rather than removing it.

proposedActions.rationale: Orphan; needed before it can be cited at the open part (3).

Not aid-proof: the Jack alpha-deformation is a different deformation from the folio's q-deformed Wedderburn weight and none of its hypotheses have been checked in that setting. The honest artifact is a remark at the q-Plancherel skeleton recording the Jack precedent and naming what would have to be checked (polynomiality of the q-character structure constants).
